366058.title: #P-hardness conjecture for Schubert coefficients
366058.literal_statement:
Let $\mathfrak{S}_w$ denote the Schubert polynomial indexed by a permutation $w\in S_\infty$, and define the Schubert coefficients by

$$
\mathfrak{S}_u\mathfrak{S}_v=\sum_{w\in S_\infty}c^w_{u,v}\mathfrak{S}_w.
$$

Writing $\operatorname{sc}_{\mathrm{Schubert}}$ for the function that computes $c^w_{u,v}$, **Schubert-coefficient hardness conjecture.** $\operatorname{sc}_{\mathrm{Schubert}}$ is $\#P$-hard. Schubert coefficients generalize Littlewood–Richardson coefficients and have geometric and algebraic interpretations. The paper describes this as a wide-open conjecture; a combinatorial interpretation, equivalently membership of the counting function in $\#P$, is also presented as a major open problem.

366059.title: Non-membership conjecture for Schubert coefficients in #P
366059.literal_statement:
Let $\mathfrak{S}_w$ denote the Schubert polynomial indexed by $w\in S_\infty$, and define $c^w_{u,v}$ by

$$
\mathfrak{S}_u\mathfrak{S}_v=\sum_{w\in S_\infty}c^w_{u,v}\mathfrak{S}_w.
$$

Writing $\operatorname{sc}_{\mathrm{Schubert}}$ for the function computing these coefficients, **Schubert non-membership conjecture.** $\operatorname{sc}_{\mathrm{Schubert}}$ is not in $\#P$. Whether Schubert coefficients have a combinatorial interpretation is a major open problem, and the paper identifies this conjecture as the opposite direction to the open $\#P$-hardness conjecture. It notes that the conjecture would follow from the unary-input contingency-table conjecture, while the cited argument claiming hardness via Littlewood–Richardson coefficients is erroneous.

366106.title: TxGraffiti's claw-free graph zero forcing conjecture
366106.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. The parameters $Z(G)$ and $Z_+(G)$ denote the standard and positive semidefinite zero forcing numbers of $G$, respectively. A graph is **claw-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,3}$. **TxGraffiti's conjecture.** If $G$ is claw-free, then

$$
Z_+(G)=Z(G).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the greater flexibility of positive semidefinite forcing does not reduce the forcing number for claw-free graphs. It is presented as a conjecture generated by the TxGraffiti conjecturing program; its resolution is not established in the supplied source.

366131.title: Hliněný's higher-genus non-orientable cover conjecture
366131.literal_statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a connected compact non-orientable surface without boundary. A **finite $\Sigma$-cover** is a finite cover of a connected graph that embeds in $\Sigma$. **Hliněný's conjecture.** A connected graph has a finite $\Sigma$-cover if and only if it is embeddable in $\Sigma$. Hliněný proposed this as a higher-genus extension of Negami's conjecture; it remains open, while the paper discusses partial progress and obstructions to analogous statements for orientable surfaces.

366132.title: The orientable higher-genus extension of Negami's conjecture
366132.literal_statement: Let $\Sigma$ be an orientable surface of Euler genus $g$, and let a **finite $\Sigma$-cover** mean a finite cover of a connected graph that embeds in $\Sigma$. **Orientable higher-genus conjecture.** A connected graph has a finite $\Sigma$-cover if and only if it is embeddable in $\Sigma$ or embeddable in the non-orientable surface of genus $g/2+1$. This is motivated by the fact that the relevant orientable surface covers itself and the corresponding non-orientable surface; the conjecture is presented as a natural analogue and remains open.

366185.title: Action of the word-deletion operator on back-stable key polynomials
366185.literal_statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a composition, let $\eta(\alpha)=\\{i\mid\nexists j<i,\alpha_j=\alpha_i\\}$, and let $\delta_i$ be the composition that is $1$ at index $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. Composition addition and subtraction are componentwise. Let $\overleftarrow{\kappa}_\alpha$ denote the back-stable key polynomial, and let $\xi$ be the operator that removes the first letter of a word.

**Key-polynomial operator conjecture.** For any composition $\alpha$,

$$
\xi(\overleftarrow{\kappa}_\alpha)=\sum_{i\in\eta(\alpha)}\overleftarrow{\kappa}_{\alpha-\delta_i}.
$$

The formula predicts an explicit action of $\xi$ on the back-stable key basis. The supplied text gives no evidence of resolution, so it is recorded as open.

366410.title: Odd-region obstruction conjecture for optimal 1-embedded graphs
366410.literal_statement: Let $G$ be an optimal $1$-embedded graph on the torus or the Klein bottle. Let $Q(G)$ denote its quadrangulation, and call a region **odd weighted** when its associated weight is odd. **Odd-region obstruction conjecture.** If $Q(G)$ has no quadrangulation as a subgraph each of whose face corresponds to an odd weighted region of $G$, then $G$ is $1$-extendable. The paper notes that such quadrangulations provide obstructions to extendability and proposes this condition as sufficient for $1$-extendability on the torus or Klein bottle; its resolution is not supplied here.

366446.title: Gallai's conjecture for chordal graphs with subdivided caterpillar representations
366446.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected chordal graph admitting a tree representation $T$, where $T$ is a subdivided caterpillar. **Subdivided-caterpillar Gallai conjecture.** Then

$$
\mathrm{lpt}(G)=1.
$$

This asserts that every such graph has a single-vertex longest path transversal. It is a restricted version of the broader open problem asking whether every connected chordal graph satisfies $\mathrm{lpt}(G)=1$; the supplied text does not state whether this restricted claim is resolved.

367723.title: The permutational Boone–Higman conjecture
367723.literal_statement: Let a group $\Gamma$ act faithfully on a set $S$. The action is of **type (A)** if $\Gamma$ is finitely presented, every stabilizer $\operatorname{Stab}_{\Gamma}(s)$ is finitely generated, and the diagonal action on $S\times S$ has finitely many orbits. **Permutational Boone–Higman conjecture.** Every finitely generated group with solvable word problem embeds in a group admitting an action of type (A), and hence in a finitely presented simple twisted Brin–Thompson group. This strengthens the Boone–Higman conjecture by requiring the embedding to arise from an action whose associated twisted Brin–Thompson group is finitely presented and simple; the paper proves this stronger property for several families, while the general conjecture remains open.

371549.title: Hamidoune's bounded symmetric-exchange conjecture
371549.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r$, and let $(A,B)$ and $(A',B')$ be compatible basis pairs, meaning that

$$
A\cap B=A'\cap B'\qquad\text{and}\qquad A\cup B=A'\cup B'.
$$

A **symmetric exchange** is an exchange of elements between the two bases that leaves both resulting sets as bases. **Hamidoune's conjecture.** For any compatible basis pairs $(A,B)$ and $(A',B')$ in a rank-$r$ matroid, the first pair can be transformed into the second using at most $r$ symmetric exchanges. This optimization variant unifies the disjoint-bases transformation proposed by Gabow with White's compatibility question; the source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

374596.title: Balogh–Clemen–Lidický conjecture on the balanced bipartite distance of $K_4$-free graphs
374596.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices. The **Balogh–Clemen–Lidický conjecture.** $G$ can be made balanced bipartite by removing at most

$$
\frac{n^2}{9}
$$

edges.
This conjecture asks whether the sharp bipartite-distance bound for $K_4$-free graphs matches the bound suggested by the complete tripartite graph. The surrounding text identifies it as a conjecture of Balogh, Clemen, and Lidický; no resolution is given here.

374717.title: Circuit characterization of distance reduction for toric ideals of graphs
374717.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $A_G$ be its incidence matrix, let $I_G$ be the corresponding toric ideal, and let $M$ be a minimal Markov basis for $I_G$. A Markov basis is **distance-reducing** when it has the distance-reduction property for the fibers of $I_G$. **Circuit characterization conjecture.** $M$ is distance-reducing if and only if $M$ reduces the distance of the circuits of $A_G$. This conjecture asserts that, for toric ideals of graphs, it is enough to check distance reduction on circuits. It is proved in the paper when $I_G$ is a complete intersection toric ideal, while the general case remains open.

382335.title: Ehrenborg–Morel–Readdy's conjecture on pizza quantities for Coxeter arrangements
382335.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a Coxeter arrangement on a finite-dimensional inner product space $V$, let $a\in V$, and let $R$ satisfy $\|a\|\leq R$. Assume that the number of hyperplanes of $\mathcal{H}$ is greater than $\dim(V)$ and has parity different from $\dim(V)$. **Ehrenborg–Morel–Readdy's conjecture.** The pizza quantity $P(\mathcal{H},\mathbb{B}(a,R))$ is zero if and only if the center $a$ lies on one of the hyperplanes of $\mathcal{H}$. This conjecture addresses the parity cases not covered by the known vanishing theorem; the supplied text does not establish the assertion, so its resolution remains open.

357132.title: Periodic density conjecture for directed sequences
357132.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be an infinite periodic sequence over the alphabet $\{1,2\}$, and let $\mathcal{O}_T$ be its directed sequence. Denote by $d_1(T)$ and $d_1(\mathcal{O}_T)$ the densities of $1$'s in $T$ and $\mathcal{O}_T$, respectively. **Periodic density conjecture.** The density of $1$'s in $\mathcal{O}_T$ is well-defined and satisfies

$$
d_1(\mathcal{O}_T)=d_1(T).
$$

This extends Keane's conjecture from deterministic directing sequences to the periodic case. Simulations support the assertion, while the general periodic case remains unproved in the supplied text.

357186.title: Weak Mittleman's conjecture for the Dirac–Fock ground state energy
357186.literal_statement:
Let $e_q$ be the physical ground state energy of the electron-positron Hartree–Fock model and let $E_q$ be the ground state energy of the Dirac–Fock model. For $alpha$ small and $c$ large, the two energies satisfy

$$
e_q\leq E_q\leq e_q+o_{\alpha_c\to 0}(c^{-2}).
$$

**Weak Mittleman's conjecture.** The Dirac–Fock model is an approximation of the electron-positron Hartree–Fock model in the precise sense of the displayed inequality. This weaker statement is introduced because the original conjecture may fail when the relevant eigenvalue is not simple or when the stated spectral-gap condition does not hold. It quantifies the error at order smaller than $c^{-2}$ in the indicated nonrelativistic regime.

357238.title: Localized hypergraph clique-weight conjecture
357238.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a $q$-uniform hypergraph with $m$ edges, let $\K(\mathcal{H})$ denote its collection of cliques, and let $t\geq q>i\geq 1$. For each $I\in\binom{V(\mathcal{H})}{i}$, define $x(I)\geq q-i-1$ by

$$
d(I)=\binom{x(I)-i}{q-i},
$$

and for each $T\in\K(\mathcal{H})$ define

$$
x(T)=\max\{x(I):I\in\binom{T}{i}\},\qquad s'(T)=\frac{1}{\binom{x(T)-q}{t-q}}.
$$

**Localized hypergraph clique-weight conjecture.** One has

$$
\sum_{T\in\K(\mathcal{H})}s'(T)\leq\frac{m}{\binom{t}{q}}.
$$

This is proposed as a localized version of a theorem of Kirsch and Radcliffe for hypergraphs, paralleling the paper's localized clique bounds. The supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or refuted.

357265.title: The bound on lengths of perfectly clustering words in Gessel's map
357265.literal_statement:
Let $n\geqslant 2$ and let $(\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_n)$ be an $(n-1)$-tuple of nonnegative integers. $$
\left\lceil\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture concerns the possible lengths of the conjugacy classes arising from the map $\Phi$ and was expressed in the second author's thesis. Its resolution is not specified in the source.

357397.title: The divisibility conjecture for morphisms of n-circular bayonet codes
357397.literal_statement:
Let an $n$-cbc $X$ be a bayonet code of the type defined in the source, and let $d$ be an integer prime to $n$. For integers $d,j,n$, let $\overline{dj}^{n}$ denote the representative of $dj$ modulo $n$. Define

$$
\varphi_d(X):=\left\{a^i b a^{\overline{dj}^{n}}\text{ such that }a^i b a^j\in X\right\}.
$$

**Divisibility conjecture for n-circular bayonet codes.** For any $n$-cbc $X$ and any $d$ prime to $n$, the set $\varphi_d(X)$ is an $n$-cbc.

The source says that this conjecture was proposed in earlier work and places it in the study of divisibility conditions for an $n$-cbc containing a given bayonet code. No resolution is supplied in the provided text.
